reason: Counted and confirmed, nearly to the digit. 26 gap declarations across the two built stylesheets (25 in b.css, 1 in shell.css:294). 12 distinct literal values - 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 28, 32, 48, 56, 64 - of which 7 (6, 10, 14, 18, 32, 48, 64) are not steps on --gap-hair..--gap-page (4/8/12/16/20/28/40/56/80). gap: 10px appears 9 times. All the inline strings in render-b.js are verbatim as quoted (729/755/786 gap:6px, 1345 margin-top:14px, 1519-1525 margin:0 0 10px -5px, margin-bottom:8px, margin-bottom:12px, margin:26px 0 0, margin-top:26px). audit.mjs:545 matches only (margin|padding)(-top|-right|-bottom|-left)? over the CSS list in build.mjs, so neither gap nor any inline style in the built master is reachable by it; the gate reports spaceLadder 0 and proves nothing here. The contrast is the finding: b.css calls the ladder 119 times for margin/padding and once for gap, while the tokens are literally named --gap-*. The sharpest evidence the seat did not cite: .b-barActs carries gap 10px at base, var(--gap-tight) inside .b-bar, and 10px again at >=1280 (b.css:600, 567, 1221), and .b-stepBtns/.b-editActs carry 10px then 14px at coarse pointer (719/720/770, 1338) - one element, several unnamed values per context, which is verbatim the defect the ladder's own comment says it retired ('one element carrying four different margins in four contexts'). Against the brief's requirement that the winner be extractable as a small named language (brief.md:68), a ladder that does not govern the property it is named after is not extractable: Home, Notes and Tasks would inherit nine names and twelve numbers. Two imprecisions that do not move the verdict: two gap lines touch a token, not one (b.css:439 is the compound gap: var(--gap-snug) 14px); and there are three inline gap:6px blocks, not the five the proposed fix claims.
sharpenedFix: Take the regex extension, refuse half the rest. Extend audit.mjs:545 to also match gap, row-gap and column-gap, but KEEP the /off-ladder/ annotation. All five of its uses (b.css:128, 817, 1226, 1239, 1241) are annotated 'measure geometry' - the 110px lane offset, the 88px editor inset, 124px, and the 110/56/120 and 100/56/110 empty and ended paddings. Those are the rail's measured geometry, not rhythm; forcing them onto nine rhythm steps would visibly move the count away from the rail and is the one change proposed here that would make the work worse. Drop the exemption only if the counter-proposal is a second, separately named geometry ladder, which is more names, not fewer. Then fix by role rather than by nearest step: give .b-barActs, .b-stepBtns, .b-editActs and .b-emptyForm one control-row token (the 9 gap:10px sites plus the 14px coarse-pointer override are the same relationship at two sizes - name it once and let the coarse-pointer rule step it, not redefine it), and settle 6 to hair(4) or tight(8), 18 to item(20), 32 to block(28), 48 and 56 to major(56), 64 to page(80) as deliberate choices, since every one of those moves layout. Move the three inline display:grid;gap:6px blocks onto a .b-editGroup class and the states.loading skeleton dimensions onto .b-skel[data-slot] rules so the source check can see them at all. Re-run interaction-check.mjs after: nine gap changes plus the 26px/14px skeleton rhythm shift the loading and editor geometry the behaviour gate measures.
